title: DP World extends Luanda concession to 2051 and plans $90m expansion
valueBasis: Additional planned investment over two years; not acquisition value
facts: A 10-year extension takes the concession to 2051.
DP World announced another $90 million of investment over two years.
Planned terminal capacity is 1.2 million TEU.
The expansion includes three ship-to-shore cranes and 12 semi-automated RTGs.
analysis: The extension adds contracted operating life, while new capex creates a cash outflow before capacity produces earnings. Model incremental demand and cash flow rather than treating design capacity as revenue.

innovation.mechanism: Additional quay and yard handling capacity can relieve operational constraints if demand and connecting infrastructure support utilization.
innovation.proof: The announced reduction in vessel turnaround is a target, not verified operating performance.

title: Hapag-Lloyd agrees to acquire 25% of Maasvlakte II
facts: Hapag-Lloyd is to acquire a 25% stake.
Completion is subject to relevant authority and regulatory approvals.
Financial terms were not disclosed.
analysis: A shipping line buying terminal equity may improve network access. Examine minority protections and whether volume commitments create measurable value.

title: APM Terminals takes a minority position alongside DP World
facts: APM Terminals will acquire 37.5% of Southern Container Terminal.
DP World will retain 62.5% and operational leadership.
DP World secured a 30-year BOT concession in 2019.
analysis: A finite concession makes the remaining cash-flow life central to valuation. Minority ownership does not automatically imply operating control.

title: DP World outlines a 50-year Fujairah concession
facts: An agreement in principle covers a 50-year concession.
The two planned assets are Al Rugaylat and Dibba terminals.
analysis: Underwrite construction, demand ramp-up and concession conditions separately. An agreement in principle is earlier than financial close.

title: DP World plans a €48m cold-chain hub in Antwerp
valueBasis: Initial project investment; not acquisition EV
facts: Initial investment is €48 million.
Later phases could bring long-term investment to around €100 million.
The planned site covers 83,000 square metres next to Antwerp Gateway.
analysis: Compare initial spend with stabilized rent or logistics margin. Do not count the €48m and €100m as two separate deals.

title: EIB provides €100m for Klaipėda’s port transformation
facts: The EIB financing is €100 million.
The overall project costs around €201 million.
Works include shoreside electricity, hydrogen facilities and offshore wind infrastructure.
analysis: Debt is a funding source, not the asset valuation. Test which cash flows repay the loan and how grants change the equity requirement.

innovation.mechanism: Grid connections and low-emission infrastructure can change energy costs and commercial capability.
innovation.proof: A financed programme is not proof of realized savings. Request utilization, tariff and commissioning evidence.

title: Partners Group’s secondaries strategy returns to atNorth
valueBasis: New stake price undisclosed; prior sale EV $4bn
facts: Partners Group’s secondaries strategy will acquire around 10%.
The prior sale to CPP Investments and Equinix valued the company at $4 billion enterprise value.
The September release says the prior transaction has closed.
analysis: Ten percent of enterprise value is not the price of 10% equity. Deduct net debt and review the capital structure and valuation date.

title: Macquarie agrees to acquire the remaining 50% of Last Mile
facts: MAM-managed funds agreed to acquire a further 50% from Infracapital.
The proposed transaction would take ownership to 100%.
The announcement expected closing in 2026, subject to conditions.
analysis: Compare connection growth, recurring network income and the capex needed for each new customer. Refresh the closing status before an interview.

title: Larger quay cranes arrive at DP World Southampton
facts: DP World announced the arrival of two large quay cranes at Southampton.
analysis: Bigger equipment creates value only if vessel demand and yard capacity support higher productive throughput.

innovation.mechanism: Higher vessel-handling capability can relieve a berth bottleneck.
innovation.proof: Arrival does not establish commissioning, productivity improvement or an investment return.
